You're absolutely right to dislike this solution: it is too terse and leaves the key counting unexplained. In particular, it should clarify why there are \(2(n-1)\) unit squares, \(n-2\) axis-aligned \(2\times2\) squares, and \(n-2\) rotated squares of side length \(\sqrt2\). Once those counts are justified, the equation is correct:
\[
2(n-1)+(n-2)+(n-2)=70,
\]
giving \(4n-6=70\), so \(\boxed{n=19}\).
